name: Pet Supplies Checklist
description: A general pet supplies checklist organized by category for anyone bringing home a new animal.

items.text: Species- and age-appropriate food
items.note: Match life stage; ask the breeder, shelter or vet what the animal currently eats

items.text: Non-tip food bowl
Fresh water bowl or bottle
Treats suitable for the species
Airtight food storage container
Measuring scoop or cup for portion control
Bed, crate, cage or enclosure sized for the animal
Soft blanket or washable liner
Hiding spot or covered area for security
Appropriate substrate or bedding material
Brush or comb suited to the coat or species
Pet-safe shampoo if bathing is needed
Nail clippers or trimming tool
Towels reserved for the pet
Ear and eye cleaning supplies if recommended
Pet first-aid kit
Flea, tick or parasite prevention if advised
items.note: Confirm the right product with a veterinarian

items.text: Carrier or transport box for vet visits
Cleaning and odor-control supplies for accidents
List of emergency vet and poison-control contacts
ID tag with your name and phone number
Collar, harness or leg band as appropriate
Microchip registration kept up to date
Recent photo of the pet in case it goes missing
Toys appropriate for the species and size
Chews or foraging items if suitable
Training pads, clicker or reward treats
Scratching, climbing or exercise gear as relevant

faq.q: What pet supplies should I buy before bringing an animal home?
faq.a: At minimum, have food, fresh water, food and water bowls, a bed or shelter, basic grooming tools and an identification method ready before the pet arrives. Species-specific items like litter, hay or a tank come next.

faq.q: How much should I budget for new pet supplies?
faq.a: Budgets vary widely by species and size, but plan for an upfront cost covering equipment plus an ongoing monthly cost for food and consumables. Buy the essentials first and add comfort items over time.

faq.q: Do I need to buy everything at once?
faq.a: No. Prioritize food, water, shelter and safety items for day one, then add grooming, enrichment and training supplies in the first week or two as you learn the animal's needs.

faq.q: Should I ask a vet before buying pet supplies?
faq.a: This checklist is general guidance. For diet, supplements or any health products, consult a veterinarian, and for exotic pets research species-specific needs before you buy.

faq.q: Can I print this pet supplies checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can carry it while shopping and check off each category as you go.
